comment: The engine's allowed unsafe items (no-cliffs C-2c-ii scope r4 section 1.3): scripts/unsafe-inventory.mjs --check compares them with the tree. hash: sha256 of the item's tokens (its outer attributes included; comments and layout excluded). audit: the answer to the boundary question for that item; a new or changed item needs a fresh review and audit.

premises.external_proc_macros_audit: Trusted dependencies (scope r4: external crates and their macro expansions are the trusted boundary). The compiler sweep can't see their expansions (rustc treats them as external), so the exact name/version set is pinned: a new proc-macro dependency or a version change fails until reviewed.

engine/flint/build.rs.audit: Emits only cargo link directives (link-search, static/dylib libs); writes no Rust source and nothing is include!d. Test-only crate (never in a shipped graph).

engine/node/build.rs.audit: napi_build::setup() only: N-API link arguments; writes no Rust source, and engine/node has no include!.

premises.no_ledger_dep_audit: Checked per crate from its manifest (any dependency section, any name); with no re-export of sagebrush_ledger anywhere (also checked), a crate on this list cannot name a ledger type.
premises.compile_time_closure_audit: The trusted external-macro boundary (scope r4): code that generates or shapes our crates' code at build time, i.e. the external proc-macro crates, the members' build dependencies, and everything they depend on, pinned by name, version, source (crates.io only) and Cargo.lock checksum. Their expansions into our crates (pyo3/napi glue) are excluded from item enumeration only inside this pinned set; a new crate, a version, source or checksum change fails until reviewed.
premises.verified_toolchain_audit: The compiler sweep's coverage (force-warn reports local macro_rules, local proc-macro and include! expansions, but not external proc-macro glue) was verified on this compiler (VM1 controls K0-K4). A toolchain bump fails this check until those controls are re-run on the new compiler.
premises.compile_views: host --workspace --all-targets (minus the test-only FLINT crates); --all-features for ledger, interrupt, poly, py; wasm32 web, raster, wasmheap, growth-probe; x86_64-pc-windows-msvc interrupt. A declared set: a new cfg or target with unsafe-relevant code must be added to scripts/unsafe-sweep.sh.

items.item: impl < A : GlobalAlloc > GlobalAlloc for Audit < A >
items.audit: Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. The audit allocator (feature ledger-audit, tests/CI only) forwards to the inner allocator; it reads the thread's CHAIN and COVER cells and the O/RES mirror atomics and writes only its own counters. It constructs, moves or mutates no ledger object; it is not generic over any ledger type.

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. sagebrush-modsym (deps: bigint, interrupt, par, poly, ap) does not depend on sagebrush-ledger directly, and no crate re-exports a ledger type (par only uses them privately), so it cannot name those types, and it reinterprets an i64 slice as u64 / calls an AVX2-compiled copy of a safe kernel, on its own numeric slices. (Premises machine-checked by scripts/unsafe-inventory.mjs: premises.no_ledger_dep against the manifests, no ledger re-export anywhere, and the pinned proc-macro/build-script closure.)

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. sagebrush-mp (deps: interrupt, wasmheap and sagebrush-bigint with dashu and num-bigint, none of which depends on the ledger; its own wasm module) does not depend on sagebrush-ledger, so it cannot name those types. No. sagebrush-nd (deps: par, optional and native only) does not depend on sagebrush-ledger, so it cannot name those types; this item is compiled only on x86_64 and touches f64 slices only. Its one unsafe operation is the call to the #[target_feature(enable = "avx2,fma")] function avx2_fma_8x6, whose only precondition is that the CPU has AVX2 and FMA. The proof is its by-value Avx2Fma argument: Avx2Fma has a private field, so the only way to make one is Avx2Fma::detect(), which returns Some only when std::is_x86_feature_detected! reports both avx2 and fma. The slices come from the safe blocking layer (Micro::tile slices them to kc * 8 and kc * 6). (Premises machine-checked by scripts/unsafe-inventory.mjs: premises.no_ledger_dep against the manifests, no ledger re-export anywhere, and the pinned proc-macro/build-script closure.)

No. sagebrush-nd (deps: par, optional and native only) does not depend on sagebrush-ledger, so it cannot name those types; this item is compiled only on x86_64 and touches no memory itself. Its one unsafe operation is the call to the #[target_feature(enable = "avx2")] function with_avx2, whose only precondition is that the CPU has AVX2. The proof is its by-value self, an Avx2Fma: Avx2Fma has a private field, so the only way to make one is Avx2Fma::detect(), which returns Some only when std::is_x86_feature_detected! reports both avx2 and fma (the same proof as avx2_fma_tile). `f` is safe Rust (a closure over the safe small-n loops of lu.rs: getf2b_on, lower_unit_pairs, upper_pairs); enabling AVX2 lets the compiler use wider instructions for it, it doesn't change what `f` may do. Only AVX2 is enabled, not FMA, and Rust never contracts a multiply and an add, so the bits are unchanged (lu::tests::the_avx2_leaves_give_the_baseline_bits). (Premises machine-checked by scripts/unsafe-inventory.mjs: premises.no_ledger_dep against the manifests, no ledger re-export anywhere, and the pinned proc-macro/build-script closure.)

The only export that writes memory. Dynamically checked in safe code (engine/nd/src/boundary.rs check, native-tested with wasm32's limits) before any pointer is read or slice made: the descriptor is 4-aligned and in the host's part of memory; every nonempty region (descriptor, A, B, C, scratch) starts at or above __heap_base (so never at 0 and never on the module's statics or linker stack), is aligned, ends within memory.size and is at most isize::MAX bytes, all in 64-bit checked arithmetic; C and the scratch lie in the job's writable arena, which the descriptor lies outside; C and the scratch overlap neither A, B nor each other; the stride holds scratch_len; the calling thread's frame lies below the arena. Pointers are made with with_exposed_provenance(_mut) from the checked absolute addresses (the host's part of linear memory is foreign memory, as across FFI), never by offsetting a null pointer; empty regions become empty slices. A refused job returns 0 having written nothing. Trusted-host preconditions (stated on the function in this wording, asserted by the page's layout): All participant stacks are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from module-owned memory, descriptor/control, A/B, and the writable arena; the host and other jobs leave all job ranges untouched until join, apart from each participant owning only its assigned C columns and scratch slot. Each thread of a job gets the same descriptor and a distinct id, so its columns of C (partition, in blocks of the module's kernel's NR, fixed per module) and its scratch slot are its own; each call checks that its own current frame lies below the arena. (Premises machine-checked by scripts/unsafe-inventory.mjs: premises.no_ledger_dep against the manifests, no ledger re-export anywhere, and the pinned proc-macro/build-script closure.)

The second export that writes memory (numerics-core P2b-1 and P2b-2, in the descriptor's mode, gesv or MATLAB: X = A \ B on one thread: the structure pass, then the diagonal, triangular, Cholesky or LU path, and rcond). Pointers are made with with_exposed_provenance(_mut) from the checked absolute addresses; empty regions become empty slices. The solve itself (solve::solve, through chol, cond and lu) is safe Rust on those slices and re-checks every span. A refused job returns 0 having written nothing, the report included.
